business_model.claim: Smithfield Foods, Inc. produces packaged meats and fresh pork products primarily in the United States and is a majority-owned subsidiary of Hong Kong-based WH Group Limited.
quotes: Headquartered in Smithfield, Virginia, since 1936, Smithfield Foods, Inc., together with its subsidiaries (“Smithfield,” “the Company,” “we,” “us” or “our”), produces a wide variety of packaged meats and fresh pork products primarily in the United States (“U.S.”).
Smithfield is a majority owned subsidiary of Hong Kong-based WH Group Limited (“WH Group”).
industry: Packaged Foods

business_model.claim: The company conducts its operations through reportable segments Packaged Meats, Fresh Pork, and Hog Production, alongside Mexico and Bioscience operating segments aggregated as Other.
quotes: We conduct our operations through three reportable segments: Packaged Meats, Fresh Pork and Hog Production.
We also conduct operations through our Mexico and Bioscience operating segments, which are aggregated and reported as “Other.”

business_model.claim: The Packaged Meats segment processes fresh meat into branded and private-label products—such as bacon, sausage, hot dogs, deli meats, and hams—for U.S. retail and foodservice customers, sourcing approximately 80% of its raw materials from Fresh Pork.
quotes: The Packaged Meats segment consists of our U.S. operations that process fresh meat into a wide variety of packaged meats products, including bacon, sausage, hot dogs, deli and lunch meats, dry sausage products (such as pepperoni and genoa salami), ham products, ready-to-eat products and prepared foods (such as bacon, sausage and pre-cooked entrées).
Approximately 80% of the Packaged Meats segment’s raw materials are sourced from our Fresh Pork segment.
We also sell a sizeable portion of our packaged meats products as private label products.
The majority of the Packaged Meats segment’s products are sold to retail and foodservice customers in the U.S.

business_model.claim: Packaged Meats is the primary earnings driver, contributing 56% of consolidated sales and 85% of overall operating profit in fiscal year 2025.
quotes: Our Packaged Meats segment is core to our growth strategy and has been a major driver in transforming our business since 2014.
The segment contributed 56% of our sales and 85% of our overall operating profit in fiscal year 2025.

business_model.claim: The Fresh Pork segment processes live hogs into primal, sub-primal, and offal cuts, sourcing approximately 40% of its hogs from Hog Production and the rest from U.S. partner farmers, while transferring approximately one-third of its output to Packaged Meats and selling the remainder externally.
quotes: The Fresh Pork segment consists of our U.S. operations that process live hogs into a wide variety of primal, sub-primal and offal products, such as bellies, butts, hams, loins, picnics and ribs.
The Fresh Pork segment sources approximately 40% of its raw materials from our Hog Production segment, with the remainder from farmers with whom we partner across the U.S.
Approximately one-third of our fresh pork products, including the majority of hams, bellies and trimmings, is transferred to our Packaged Meats segment.

Externally, we sell our fresh pork products to domestic retail, foodservice and industrial customers, as well as to export markets, including, among others, Mexico, China, Japan, South Korea and Canada.

business_model.claim: The Hog Production segment raises hogs on company-owned and contract farms primarily for Fresh Pork processing and externally sells livestock feed, grains, transportation, and ancillary services.
quotes: The Hog Production segment consists of our hog production operations in the U.S., which produce and raise our hogs on numerous Company-owned farms and farms that are owned and operated by contract farmers.
Nearly all of the hogs produced by this segment are processed by our Fresh Pork segment.
The Hog Production segment also sells livestock feed and grains and provides transportation and other ancillary services to external customers.

business_model.claim: Other operations include a 66% interest in Altosano in Mexico, which produces 1.8 million hogs annually and sells fresh pork locally, and Bioscience in Ohio, which turns hog raw materials into heparin active pharmaceutical ingredients for healthcare customers.
quotes: In Mexico, we own a 66% interest in Granjas Carroll de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V. (commonly known as “Altosano”), which raises hogs and produces fresh pork products that are sold primarily to customers in Mexico.
Our Mexico operations produce 1.8 million hogs annually at 134 company-owned farms and processes 1.4 million hogs at one manufacturing plant.

Our Bioscience manufacturing location in Ohio processes raw materials from hogs that we process to manufacture heparin products, including Heparin Sodium, an active pharmaceutical ingredient, which mitigates the risk of blood clots.
These intermediate products are sold to the healthcare industry for use in pharmaceutical drugs and medical devices.

business_model.claim: Smithfield sold to approximately 4,300 customers in fiscal year 2025, with Walmart Inc. representing approximately 15% of consolidated sales and the top ten customers representing 42%.
quotes: In fiscal year 2025, we sold our products to approximately 4,300 customers.

Walmart Inc., including its subsidiary Sam’s West, Inc. (collectively “Walmart”), is a customer of our Packaged Meats and Fresh Pork segments and accounted for approximately 15%, 16% and 15% of our consolidated sales in fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.claim: Packaged Meats revenue growth relies on brand equity, household penetration, price points, product innovation, and shifting mix toward value-added products, reinforced by the October 26, 2026 acquisition of Nathan’s Famous for $102.00 per share in cash.
quotes: Within the Packaged Meats segment, the primary factors impacting sales of our brands are household penetration, consumption levels, price point and product offerings.
We have shifted our portfolio towards a higher mix of value-added and margin accretive products while leveraging the breadth of our offerings to further penetrate across dayparts.

business_model.claim: Upstream revenues in Fresh Pork and Hog Production fluctuate with global pork demand, USDA cut-out values, CME lean hog prices, and feed sales to external partners, with softer pork commodity markets contributing to an 8.3% year-over-year drop in third-quarter 2026 consolidated sales to $3,437 (table in millions) and a Fresh Pork operating loss of $(89) (table in millions).
quotes: In our Fresh Pork segment, the primary drivers of external sales are global demand for pork, our ability to maximize the value of each hog and our ability to leverage our different end markets including retail, foodservice, industrial and export channels.

“We reported third quarter adjusted operating profit within the range we provided in September, led by strong results in our cornerstone Packaged Meats segment, with our upstream segments challenged by lower pork commodity markets,” said Smithfield President and CEO Shane Smith.

business_model.claim: Raw materials—principally hogs, fresh pork, and animal feed ingredients such as corn and soybean meal—make up the largest share of cost of goods sold, with animal feed accounting for approximately 60% of Hog Production cost of goods sold.
quotes: Raw materials are the largest component of our total cost of goods sold, with feed ingredients and hogs accounting for the majority share.
Approximately 60% of the Hog Production segment’s cost of goods sold is from animal feed, which is derived primarily from corn and soybean meal.

business_model.claim: Operating profitability is exposed to commodity price cycles—where Hog Production gains from high hog and low feed prices while downstream processing faces margin pressure when raw material costs rise faster than customer pricing—which Smithfield manages through commodity hedging, forward purchasing, and cost pass-through.
quotes: Our Hog Production segment generally generates higher profits when hog prices are high and feed ingredient prices are low, and lower profits (or losses) when hog prices are low and feed ingredient prices are high.
Competitive considerations and customer resistance to price increases may delay or make us unable to adjust our selling prices.
We enter into hedging transactions for commodities such as feed ingredients, hogs and fuel when we determine conditions are appropriate to mitigate the inherent price risks.
While this hedging may limit our ability to participate in gains from favorable commodity fluctuations, it also reduces the risk of loss from adverse changes in raw material prices.

business_model.claim: Through Hog Production Reform, Smithfield cut internal hog production from 17.6 million head in 2019 to 11.1 million head in 2025, transitioning farms to external contract suppliers such as Murphy Family Farms (approximately 3.2 million hogs annually) and VisionAg (approximately 600,000 hogs annually).
quotes: We have reduced the size of our internal hog production from a peak of 17.6 million head in 2019 to 11.1 million head in 2025, which represents approximately 40% of the hogs processed by our Fresh Pork segment.
Murphy Family Farms is now a hog supplier to us and supplies approximately 3.2 million hogs annually.
VisionAg is now a hog supplier to us and supplies approximately 600,000 hogs annually.

business_model.claim: To lower manufacturing and distribution costs across its 38 processing plants in 18 states, Smithfield invests in plant automation, facility and office consolidations, workforce reductions, and transportation and cold-storage optimization.
quotes: We manufacture packaged meats, fresh pork and value-added items at 38 processing plants across 18 different states:
We are pursuing best-in-class manufacturing principles in our plants by employing automation to redeploy labor to higher value tasks, increasing yields and driving efficiency by reducing complexity.

In our logistics and distribution network, we actively manage transportation and warehousing costs by evaluating transportation carrier mix, optimizing transportation routes, maximizing utilization of our cold storage and trucking assets, improving supply and demand planning and optimizing inventory levels.

On February 6, 2026, we announced our decision to exit our leased Springfield, Massachusetts dry sausage production facility by the end of August 2026 and consolidate production across our network, including at our recently acquired Nashville, Tennessee facility.

business_model.claim: Operating costs are also influenced by fuel and energy price volatility affecting freight and inputs, as well as SG&A litigation charges ($80 million in fiscal year 2025 and $13 million in fiscal 2026 through September 27, 2026).
quotes: Energy prices directly influence freight, logistics and certain raw material costs across our supply chain, which have increased and may continue to increase our operating costs.
Charges totaling $80 million were recorded in fiscal year 2025 and are included in selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) in the consolidated statements of income.
